\label{thm:ttstratificationuniversality}
Suppose $\cat T$ is BIK-stratified by the action of a graded commutative Noetherian ring $R$. Then $\cat T$ is stratified (\cref{def:stratification}) and there exists a canonical homeomorphism $\mathrm{Supp}^{R \circlearrowright \cat T}(\cat T) \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)$. Under this homeomorphism, $\mathrm{Supp}^{R \circlearrowright \cat T}$ coincides with the Balmer--Favi notion of support $\mathrm{Supp}$.

Moreover, if $R = [\mathbb{1},\mathbb{1}]^{\bullet}$ and $\cat T$ is stratified by the canonical action of $R$ on $\cat T$, then Balmer's comparison map \eqref{eq:Balmercomparisonmap},
\[
\xymatrix{\rho^{\bullet}\colon \mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c) \ar[r]^-{\cong} & \mathrm{Spec}^h(R),}
\]
is a homeomorphism.

The graded commutative cohomology ring of $R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ is isomorphic to a graded polynomial ring over $R$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cohomologytorus}
\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}} \cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_r],
\end{equation}
where each of the generators $x_i$ has (homological) degree $-2$. Represent these generators by maps $x_i\colon\Sigma^{-2}R \to R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ of $R$-module spectra. The induced map 
\[
\textstyle\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\Sigma^{-2}R \to R^{h\mathbb{T}}
\]
extends to a map of $\mathbb{E}_1$-$R$-algebras from the free $\mathbb{E}_1$-$R$-algebra on $\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\Sigma^{-2}R$:
\[
\mathrm{Free}_{\mathbb{E}_1-R}(x_1,\ldots,x_r) \to R^{h\mathbb{T}}.
\]
By construction, this map induces an isomorphism on homotopy groups and thus exhibits the underlying $\mathbb{E}_1$-$R$-algebra of $R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ as formal. Finally, Shipley's theorem \cite{shipley_hzalgebras} provides the translation into the language of dg-algebras.

The result follows from derived Morita theory proven by Schwede and Shipley~\cite{SS03} and Lurie~\cite[Thm.~7.1.2.1]{HALurie}, as soon as we have verified the following two claims:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{A}_P)$ is compactly generated by its unit $\underline{A}_P$;
        \item the derived endomorphisms of $\underline{A}_P$ are equivalent to $A^{hP}$, as commutative ring spectra. 
    \end{enumerate}
For the first claim, note that the unit homomorphism $\eta\colon k \to A$ induces a tt-functor
\[
\xymatrix{\eta^*\colon \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{k}_P) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{A}_P),}
\]
whose forgetful right adjoint is conservative. In particular, $\eta^*$ preserves compact generators. Since $P$ is a finite $p$-group, $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{k}_P) \simeq \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}(k^{tP})$ is compactly generated by its unit. Therefore, the same is true for $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{A}_P)$.

In order to see (2), we compute
\[
\mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{A}_P)}(\underline{A}_P) \simeq \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(S_P^0,\underline{A}_P) \simeq \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(EP_+,\mathrm{infl} A) \simeq A^{hP}.
\]
As in \cite[\S2.2]{mathew_torus}, this equivalence is compatible with the commutative ring spectra structures on both sides, which implies the claim.

Any regular commutative ring decomposes as a finite product of regular integral domains. Since the formation of the categories $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_G}(\underline{R}_G)$ commutes with finite products, we can reduce to $R$ itself being a regular domain. If $p$ is zero in $R$, then the result is a special case of \cref{prop:elabeqstratificationcharp}, so it remains to consider the case that $p \in R$ is regular.

In order to prepare for the proof, we begin with the construction of two tt-functors, $q^*$ and $f^*$, with the following two properties:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item on Balmer spectra, the functors $q^*$ and $f^*$ induce a jointly bijective map;
        \item the target categories of $q^*$ and $f^*$ are stratified. 
    \end{enumerate}
We will then argue by descent, appealing to the techniques from \cref{ssec:ttascentanddescent}.    

The quotient map $R \to R/p$ induces a morphism $q\colon \underline{R}_E \to \underline{R/p}_E$ of commutative $E$-equivariant ring spectra, and hence a colimit preserving tt-functor
\[
\xymatrix{q^*\colon\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R/p}_E).}
\]
Its forgetful right adjoint $q_*$ is conservative and preserves compact objects: Indeed, $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R/p}_E)$ is monogenic by \cref{prop:monogenicborel} and $\underline{R/p}_E \simeq \mathrm{cof}(\underline{R}_E \xrightarrow{p} \underline{R}_E)$, viewed as an $\underline{R}_E$-module, is compact. This suffices to apply \cite[Thm.~1.7]{Balmer18}, which shows that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:suppofRmodp}
    \mathrm{supp}(\underline{R/p}_E) = \mathrm{im}(\varphi);
\end{equation}
here, $\varphi\colon \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R/p}_E)) \to \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E))$ is the map on spectra induced by $q^*$. By \cref{lem:injectivity}, $\varphi = \mathrm{Spc}(q^*)$ is injective.

Consider the finite (Verdier) localization of $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E)$ away from the localizing ideal $\Loco{\underline{R/p}_E}$:
\[
\xymatrix{f^*\colon \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R[1/p]}_E).}
\]
The category of local objects is as stated, because localizing away from the cofiber of multiplication by $p$ has the effect of inverting $p$, which in turn can be performed on the level of the unit. By virtue of \cref{prop:monogenicborel} and the fact that the group cohomology ring $\pi_*R^{hE} \cong H^*(E;R)$ is $p^{\mathrm{rank}_p(E)}$-torsion in all non-zero degrees, we can identify the target of $f^*$ further as 
\[
\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R[1/p]}_E) \simeq \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}((R[1/p])^{hE}) \simeq \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}(R[1/p]).
\]
The induced injective map $\psi\colon \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}^c(R[1/p])) \to \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E))$ on spectra exhibits the domain as the quasi-compact open subset complementing $\mathrm{supp}(\underline{R/p}_E)$. Combined with \eqref{eq:suppofRmodp} this shows that $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are jointly surjective, thereby establishing Property (a) above. Property (b) holds as well, using \cref{prop:elabeqstratificationcharp} and Neeman's stratification theorem for derived categories of Noetherian commutative rings, \cite[Thm.~2.8]{Neeman92a}.

After this preparation, we can now descend stratification along $f^*$ and $q^*$. To this end, first consider a local category $\Gamma_{\frak p}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E)$ for a prime tt-ideal $\frak p \in \mathrm{im}(\psi) \subseteq \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E))$. Since $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}(R[1/p])$ is stratified, $\Gamma_{\frak p}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E)$ is minimal by Zariski descent \cref{prop:ttdescent}(1). If $\frak p \in \mathrm{im}(\varphi)$ instead, we deduce minimality of $\Gamma_{\frak p}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E)$ via \'etale descent along $f^*$, using \cref{prop:ttdescent}(2). 

Finally, it remains to observe that $\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E))$ is Noetherian and homeo-morphic to $\mathrm{Spec}^h(\pi_*R^{hE})$, thanks to Lau's theorem \cite{lau_spcdmstacks}.

nodes.statement: We offer some comments on the derived category of representations considered in this paper. Since it is rigidly-compactly generated, Rep(G,R) is determined as a symmetric monoidal category by its full subcategory of compact objects rep(G,R) = Fun(BG,Perf(R)). Its homotopy category Ho(rep(G,R)) can be identified with the following categories: item The bounded derived category of modules over R[G] whose underlying complex of R-modules is perfect. item The category of perfect complexes over the Deligne--Mumford quotient stack [Spec(R)/G], when R is a regular commutative ring equipped with trivial G-action. Furthermore, Rep(G,R) admits a canonical localization functor to the unbounded derived category D(R[G]) whose kernel is by definition our version of the stable module category StMod(G,R) with coefficients in a general commutative ring R. In fact, this localization sequence promotes to a recollement familiar from Rickard's presentation of the stable module category with field coefficients. The stable module category StMod(G,R) also admits an algebraic model; we refer to for the details. In short, let Lat(G,R) be the category of R-linear G-representations with underlying projective R-module. The category of such representations inherits a Frobenius exact structure from the abelian category Mod(R[G]) in which it is embedded. Likewise, the R-linear tensor product on Mod(R[G]) restricts to a symmetric monoidal structure on Lat(G,R). The homotopy category of the associated Quillen exact model structure is then canonically equivalent to the homotopy category of the infty-category StMod(G,R) as tt-categories.

Furthermore, Rep(G,R) admits a canonical localization functor to the unbounded derived category D(R[G]) whose kernel is by definition our version of the stable module category StMod(G,R) with coefficients in a general commutative ring R. In fact, this localization sequence promotes to a recollement familiar from Rickard's presentation of the stable module category with field coefficients. The stable module category StMod(G,R) also admits an algebraic model; we refer to for the details. In short, let Lat(G,R) be the category of R-linear G-representations with underlying projective R-module. The category of such representations inherits a Frobenius exact structure from the abelian category Mod(R[G]) in which it is embedded. Likewise, the R-linear tensor product on Mod(R[G]) restricts to a symmetric monoidal structure on Lat(G,R). The homotopy category of the associated Quillen exact model structure is then canonically equivalent to the homotopy category of the infty-category StMod(G,R) as tt-categories.
